cleared.check: ParseBytes.parseSelector (src/libraries/ParseBytes.sol:9-14) and parseFee (16-21) load a full word into a bytes4 and a uint24 without masking. Does a hook answer with nonzero bytes after the selector, a caller whose address has nonzero upper bytes (so the first calldata word carries them), or a fee word with bits above 24 change the outcome?
cleared.result: No. In the reference EVM with the driver at an address whose upper 16 bytes are nonzero and hooks that pad the selector with 0xff bytes, all ten hook functions are accepted exactly as with zero padding (out/dirtysel.json), so the compiled comparison at Hooks.sol:152 cleans both sides to 4 bytes. Fee words 2^255 | 0x400000 | 500 and 2^24 | 0x400000 | 500 behave as 0x400000 | 500, and 2^24 | 500 as no override, on all 21 networks, because isOverride and removeOverrideFlag mask (src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:61-70). Only the hook of the pool can choose these words.

cleared.check: Task 2: native value. settle with value in a native pool, settle and settleFor with value while an ERC-20 is synced, sync of native after an ERC-20 sync, settle with zero value, settleFor S, overpayment, a take above the PoolManager's balance and at 2^127, native claims, and native takes of 1 and 0 to 62 recipients (an account without code, a contract that reverts, address zero, the PoolManager itself, precompiles 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x100, and OP Stack, Arbitrum, HyperEVM, Celo, Polygon, BNB Chain, Monad, Avalanche, Arc and Tempo system addresses, EntryPoints, EIP-4788, 2935, 7002 and 7251 contracts and Permit2), on every network.
cleared.result: Every native settle case returns the reference words on every network. settle or settleFor with value while an ERC-20 is synced reverts with NonzeroNativeValue and the value stays with the caller. A take above the PoolManager's balance or at 2^127 reverts. A take to a recipient that rejects value reverts with WrappedError(NativeTransferFailed), so the debit is undone. Where a recipient has code on one network and not on another the outcome differs (listed per network in the first cleared item), and every such difference changes only whether the caller's own payout goes through or lands at that address. A take to the PoolManager itself reverts everywhere, because the contract has no receive or fallback function. No take or settle credited anyone other than the caller or the named recipient.

cleared.check: Which precompile addresses answer a value call with empty input differently from Ethereum (Prague and Osaka rules: 0x09 to 0x11 fail on empty input, EIP-2537 says an error burns all gas supplied).
cleared.result: On Avalanche and HyperEVM the addresses 0x0b to 0x11 accept the payout, so they hold no BLS12-381 precompile at the endpoint's fork, and a native take there leaves the caller's own value at that address. The call to 0x100 with empty input succeeds on these two and on Ethereum alike (checked on reth v2.11.0 and on eth.drpc.org on 2026-11-26), so it says nothing about a P-256 precompile. On Polygon 0x0a accepts the payout on the drpc gateway and on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), so bor has no point evaluation precompile there. On api.avax.network 0x0a fails with invalid input length and 0x0b accepts. On every other network these addresses fail as on Ethereum. The PoolManager neither calls precompiles itself nor reads their answers apart from the success flag of a payout the caller chose.

cleared.check: Native asset with an ERC-20 face (CELO token on Celo, USDC 0x3600..00 on Arc, 0x1010 on Polygon): sync of the face then settle with value, sync of the face then a native take then settle, a native settle before a face sync, and how the face balance follows a native payment.
cleared.result: On all three, sync(face) then settle with value reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (0xb0ec849e); sync(face), a native take of 5 and settle() reverts with Panic 0x11 at the checked subtraction of src/PoolManager.sol:360; a native settle of 7 followed by sync(face) and settle() credits 7 native and 0 face. The face balance of the PoolManager follows the native balance one to one on Celo and Polygon, and on Arc in 6 decimal units (10^27 wei shows as 10^15, and 10^12 wei more as one unit more). The face and native currency ids keep separate deltas, so a payment in one face is never credited in the other. This repeats with the hook driver what F-023, F-032, F-050 and F-008 record.

cleared.check: Native take to address zero on Arc.
cleared.result: It reverts with WrappedError(NativeTransferFailed) on Arc and succeeds on the other networks, as F-125 records for Arc's value-transfer frame hook. Only the caller's own payout is refused.

cleared.check: Monad compiled path: the 575 cases through the cycle 23 harness, interpreter against native x86 code, at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7, one world per case.
cleared.result: 562 of 575 cases (v0.16.7) and 561 (v0.16.5) give the same result in both engines and, apart from harness modelling of balances and precompiles, the reference words. All 143 native value cases agree between engines once the harness balance lines are written as 64 hex digits (the first run wrote odd-length hex, which the harness misreads). 13 hook cases differ: the native side reverts the whole unlock with empty data in 12 and the interpreter side in 1. The same PoolManager call sent alone (initialize with an afterInitialize hook that returns 1 to 31 bytes) gives InvalidHookResponse in both engines, a rebuild of the harness that only records each call's result after it returns makes 10 of the 13 agree and leaves 3 others different, and zeroing or filling the native stack changes nothing. A result that moves with host-side bookkeeping points at the harness's host process, not at Monad's EVM semantics. The root cause was not found; it is a lead.

With balance overrides the Tempo endpoint moves value inside eth_call, and all native settle cases return the reference words. Without an override, SELFBALANCE of a contract, BALANCE of 0xb0b and a value CALL of 1 give [0, 0, 0] while eth_getBalance answers 0x9612084f0316e0ebd5182f398e5195a51b5ca47667d4c9b26c9b26c9b26c9b2 (tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, block 50948840). No account holds native value in the EVM, so on the live chain settle credits msg.value 0 and every native take of a nonzero amount fails, which is the cleared Tempo answer of earlier cycles. The hook cases that failed in Tempo batches at 30 million gas return the reference words when run alone at 50 million.

leads.question: Do Avalanche and HyperEVM plan to add the EIP-2537 and P-256 precompiles at 0x0b to 0x11 and 0x100, and at which fork, so that a payout to those addresses changes from accepted to failing?
leads.why: Integrations that pay out to arbitrary addresses would see a behaviour change; no pool funds are at stake.

leadResults.answer: The four sides run on all 21 networks through the extended driver with a hook double and native balance overrides, and every network returns the reference words (Pool.sol:320, PoolManager.sol:181, PoolManager.sol:356, Currency.sol:51). No rule of Task 4 is broken.
